chapter: Rhythm and the Sam Morgan band
title: Vamping, rhythm and the Sam Morgan band's tempo
summary: He explains vamp style on trombone and the importance of a steady rhythm section, praising how Sam Morgan set the tempo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Say, can you hum a little vamp for me? I was wondering what kind of vamp you learned when Willie Foster would play the violin. They're going to play now?
Well, just hum a couple of little licks for me. Can you do it?

You're talking about the vamp style, what is that? I mean, is it the bass style? That's a vamp style. Ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba. That's a vamp, you see? They're fitting in, you know?
Like you say in Thailand Especially when a trumpet player holds a good lead like Heart Society, I'd rather vamp the part than trying to sing a solo, understand? Because it's a song much better.
I've heard you talk before years ago about the importance of the rhythm. That is, you have to have that beat on the trombone. Can you tell us about that?

Yeah, that beat. You see, that beat on the trombone. In other words, you see, when you play this language, you can't rush it. If you rush it, you can't make your chord thing good, understand? See, because you rush in those two, see? Now, especially like our band, Sam, like the band he got there now. But our band, this band never played like Sam Morgan band. Because see, Sam had a tempo. He set you to a tempo and that rhythm holds you right there. You never move. See? Because that's a whole background. Under that piano, your drum, bass, and banjo. That's your background. Now, if them people don't write together, you can go to your bands out there. You can't even get nowhere. Now, Bill, you know I'm telling the truth. Yeah, I know. You see? Now, that band, and the drum, boom, boom. You're going as fast as a cycle. You can't execute your own like you want to. It's too fast. Understand? But along that drum and that piano, that band, and bass, it must work together. Well, that's the whole thing. That's where any man got a band should get that together, that drum and bass and banjo. Understand? And piano. Because that's the main thing. That's your background. And at that clicking, your band got to go right.
Well, how would they work with Sam Morgan?

Listen, Sam was on the time because Sam had one of them slapsticks, you see? You see? And Sam would get that band to move. He'd hold that stick. Like, understand? But otherwise, the band, the father had got together, so the rhythm, he had to worry about because this dude, you knock a piece off. You couldn't move them, brother. They're still right there. You couldn't move them. No, you couldn't move them. You couldn't move them. And Sam would take any kind of number and make a really, a dance number of it. You don't care what kind of number, but he'd take it and make a dance number. He could put a time to play in a moving time that you'd like it. He was a good man for that. Otherwise, we have one of the best, I mean, swing bands in the city of New Orleans. In the world, I'll tell you that. At Sam Morgan, we had to swing to that band because otherwise, you come to that band, no care what you could play. Don't say that with the music proposition, but that swing. You ought to do that swing. You see, some brothers, they've been playing so fast, they get the swing band, they can't play like they want to. You see? You see? They don't, someone move their finger on their horn and different things, and that's, that's make it sound bad.
